agree.reason: The pre-renovation rise from 7.9 to 8.2, the seven weeks of covered shifts with overtime under plan, and a concrete budget plan give a GM who believes the renovation drove the scores real reasons to rethink, but the outside candidate's bigger-hotel experience is never really answered.

honest.reason: It drops the 'main reason' claim and its numbers are accurate, but 'the payroll budget is mostly scheduling and overtime' and the transition 'again' are claims the brief doesn't support.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns turnover into 64% to 36% and shows training time cut by nearly half, but it could have pointed out that 0.3 of the 0.7-point gain (more than 40%) came before the renovation started.

right_comparison.reason: The outside candidate is shown only by their weakness (learning a new hotel) and never by their real strength (running a larger desk), so the comparison leans one way.

qualification.reason: The budget plan names a three-month deadline and weekly controller meetings, but it gives no measurable checkpoint and says nothing about what happens if she falls short.

objections.reason: The renovation objection is answered directly with pre-renovation data and the budget gap is admitted and addressed, but the larger-hotel experience objection is avoided rather than met.

fit.reason: It's a tight one-page memo to the GM, with clear headed sections, as the brief asked.
